### comment 5999398236 — 2026-10-05T17:14:40Z — Casey-allard

# Council verdict — four independent experts, adversarial by construction

Four experts were dispatched with no shared context: a **mechanism auditor** (what is implemented, wired, measured), a **project historian** (trajectory, stalled period, roadmap), an **external expert** (literature, with web research), and a **red-team** (attack the direction). **They converged on the same four findings from four different directions**, and the convergence — not any single report — is the result.

---

## 1. The geometry is not doing measurable work. All four agree.

**Red-team, from the source.** The winning synthetic configuration is an **ordinary attention block**: `candle_nn::ops::softmax(&scores,3)?.matmul(&value)?` with a learned relative-distance bias and a no-read sink. Parameter mass of the winning arm: **SwiGLU MLP 65.1%, dense q/k/v/o 28.9%, embedding 4.8%, everything geometry-adjacent 1.13% — and the score geometry itself is 48 scalars, 0.0035%.** It sits on `ReadScore::L2`, which the code labels the *"matched flat control"* of Lorentz. In 22,633 lines, **`Hopf` occurs 0 times and `zeta` once, in a doc comment.**

**The controls already exist and they tie or invert:**

```
pattern=aaaaaa  read=l2   key_shift=NO    0.2539 / 0.0000
pattern=aaaaaa  read=dot  key_shift=NO    0.2266 / 0.0000     <- Lorentz vs dot: indistinguishable
pattern=aaaaaa  read=l2   key_shift=YES   1.0000 / 1.0000     <- ZERO r layers
pattern=rararr  read=l2   key_shift=NO    1.0000 / 1.0000
pattern=rrarra  read=l2   key_shift=NO    0.0039 / 0.0000     <- same layer multiset, same seed
pattern=rrrrrr                             0.0000 / 0.0000
```

**`rararr` vs `rrarra` is the same multiset of layers, the same parameter count, the same seed, the same data — 100% vs 0.4%.** That is a fragility result, not a mechanism result. Capability tracks `key_shift`, a signed permutation plus an add.

**Auditor, independently.** Only **one** declared geometric thing is on the production path and beats its matched alternative: quaternion transport in `r`, **+0.0234 nats, 2 seeds**. Prime/zeta/Hopf/E8 are *"identity labels or matched-control arms only."* `guarantees.rs` — `ZPhi`, `IcosianQuaternion`, `PairedH4Icosian`, `chirality`, `polarity` — has **zero non-test callers**. ~6,400 lines of prime-route attention are reachable only from tests, at **0–1/32** fresh transfer.

**Historian.** F2's geometric claim was **retracted by its own frozen rule**: identity shift 0.993/0.983, random SO(4) 0.991/0.984, learned conv 0.995/0.997, learned `W_prev` 0.996/0.985, **F2 0.995/0.984**. `j` is decorative; any shift works.

**And geometry has lost every attribution contest it has entered** (`formal_vocabulary.md`): scrambled transport **beat** real H4 by 0.033 nats; geometric-minus-pooled −0.0039; V5 +0.0239 **with worse own NLL**. The one mechanism measured load-bearing is **ordinary causal attention at 2.68 nats**.

---

## 2. The discipline cannot conclude against the geometry — and this blocks every experiment.

The red-team found this written into the normative documents:

```
DECISIONS.md:158   "a geometric mechanism is not retired on a near-zero delta"
DECISIONS.md:192   "Never retire an enabler or selector on a near-zero or NEGATIVE delta"
DECISIONS.md:438   "Gates promote; they never kill."
DECISIONS.md:443   FAIL, DEAD, RETIRED now read "not yet promoted at that scope"
formal_vocabulary:99  "Architectural load-bearing is ASSUMED"
AGENTS.md         "a failed experiment does not demote the whole architecture"
DECISIONS.md:231  "No geometric mechanism has beaten a matched ordinary control on any
                   tested task in this repository" -- and it is retained anyway
```

**D2's escape hatch nullifies D1's falsification rule.** Every mechanism can be declared `enabler` or `selector`, every miss relabelled, and *negative* deltas re-attributed to "wiring." The project's own PI-review names the consequence: mechanisms *"un-retired on policy, never re-tested — **the largest single risk to this programme**."*

**The historian reached the same place from the history:** the binding constraint was never administrative — **~400 PRs merged at a median 15 minutes, 73% touching `crates/`** — it was *"having no instrument that could falsify its own hypothesis."* Three months of score-geometry swaps on keys carrying no predecessor content, on a model handed the answer in training, on a panel blind to recall.

---

## 3. The recall barrier is FIXED — by data, not mechanism. This is the best news and the sharpest reframe.

**Verified directly from #820, 2026-10-05T08:36Z:**

| arm | MQAR, sieve OFF (network alone) |
|---|---|
| oracle curriculum, F2 off | **5/109** |
| oracle curriculum, F2 add | **1/109** |
| recall-off, high dose, F2 off | **97/109**, **106/109** |
| recall-off, high dose, F2 add | **105/109**, 101/109 |

**And Step 1c, the new best chat model `chat-100m2-balp-s1`:**

| | before | Step 1c |
|---|---|---|
| MQAR sieve OFF | 5 | **105** |
| Instruction | 71 | **77** |
| Relation | 76 | **81** |
| **Total sieve OFF** | 876 | **1004** |

All frozen acceptance criteria PASS on both seeds. **The fix was three corpus choices and no mechanism change.** The owner's instinct about supplied answers was right, and it was *literally* the root cause.

**So: recall now works. It does not work because of the geometry.** Those are different claims and conflating them is how three months were spent.

---

## 4. The serving constraint is measurably fighting the goal, and its justification has never been measured.

The red-team, from the project's own receipts:

```
energy      Integer is ~4.31x the marginal energy of float per token  (energy-qualification-20260928.md)
latency     3-5x slower than D10 NEON; 5.40 vs 1.11 ms/token
bytes       12,373,333 touched per token
cause       memory traffic -- i.e. the dense access D5 was meant to eliminate
D5          "no such mechanism is built"  |  "Zero measurements"  (DECISIONS.md:772; catalogue)
```

Only **arithmetic fidelity** is measured, and it comes back clean — 0 max logit diff, 7.79e-7 nats, 100% parity, 4.25 bpw, 27.33 MB RSS. **That proves the constraint is implementable. It does not prove it pays.**

Two audit qualifications from the mechanism auditor, worth recording: the D11 run reports **8 call-graph violations** (all `rayon`/`crossbeam` scheduler arithmetic) and exits non-zero, and the published *"FULL PASS, 0 forbidden over 44 ranges / 83 functions"* is **not reproducible** — the auditor gets 36 ranges / 139 functions. Separately, `serving_multiplier_check.py` returns **PASS vacuously** — all 12 CERTIFIED symbols report `NO SYMBOL`. **That PASS must not be cited.**

---

## THE DECISION

### Move 1 — Make the discipline able to lose. *(Owner decision; blocks everything else.)*

**Suspend D2's `enabler`/`selector` exemption and D12's "never kill" for one pre-registered geometry-attribution contest, with "geometry retired from the critical path" as a real, permitted outcome.**

D4 already states that no geometric mechanism has ever beaten a matched control here, and the mechanisms were retained anyway. **Until losing is possible, no experiment can change a decision** — which is precisely the state the historian identifies as the three-month barrier. This is the only move that makes the others matter, and it is a **governance change that requires owner authority**, not an agent's call.

### Move 2 — Run the D5 contest. *(Highest-value experiment; the project's one differentiated claim.)*

D5 — bounded candidate scoring plus exact addressed memory read in one pass — is the **only** claim a dense transformer cannot match, the **only** lever that moves energy, latency *and* bytes/token together, and it has **zero measurements** after being the terminal invariant of every result.

The contest is already specified: **geometric router vs ordinary LSH / learned-kNN at matched access budget, judged by top-K decision-equivalence.** Two outcomes are both useful, and both must be permitted: either D5 wins and the constraint is justified, or it loses and **the honest move is to serve the 4-bit dense map on the multiplier path, which is measured faster and cheaper.** The second outcome is currently unwritable.

### Move 3 — The teacher-forcing transport probe. *(Half a day; cheap and decisive.)*

Measure `P(token 2 | correct token 1)` against `P(token 2 | random token 1)`.

- **≈equal** → the payload is not addressable during continuation. Read-path problem; the external expert's literature is unambiguous that this is a **named, proven** gap ("selective copying") with a **non-attention** fix: NTM read-head shift, DNC temporal links, or stored intra-value bigrams so the existing lookup can chain.
- **correct ≫ random** → exposure bias, not architecture.

**Two hypotheses currently look identical; this separates them for half a day of compute.** And it should be run on the **new curriculum**, because the last transport measurement was taken on the oracle-curriculum model — the same confound that made 5/109 look like a mechanism failure.

---

## WHAT TO STOP

- **My own reader line (#1737).** I measured it at **0/100 on the panel's natural phrasing** — 0/100 facts and 0/100 questions resolving to a usable label — after four rounds of rules that scored 67% on *templated* forms I authored. **It is a template parser and the product needs natural language. Abandon it; do not extend it.** I would close #1737 as a component result.
- **Score-geometry swaps** while key content is unchanged — the class the synthesis names as the three-month barrier.
- **The ~6,400 test-only lines of prime-route attention**, and `guarantees.rs` (zero non-test callers). Two incompatible definitions of "geometric attention" coexist because of them.
- **Single-seed verdicts and benches whose layout makes passing a tautology.**

## WHAT IS GENUINELY WORTH KEEPING

The steelman is real and it is **not** the geometry:

1. **A multiplier-free, float-free integer engine that is bit-exact against float** — 0 logit diff, 100% parity over 1,433 decisions, 4.25 bpw, 27.33 MB RSS. Few projects have this.
2. **D5's thesis — untouched, not refuted.** Exact addressed memory in one read is a property a dense transformer cannot match. Its absence, not its failure, is why energy is 4.31× against.
3. **F2 lineage as a deployable primitive** — a signed permutation plus an add, D11-legal, 0.25 → 1.00 on synthetic MQAR. Whether it is *geometric* is branding; that it is a cheap exact integer induction operator is measured.
4. **An unusually strong falsification apparatus** — `lorentz|dot|l2` and `Quaternion|U1` are parameter-matched same-kernel controls, and the `none/f2/qk/identity/so4/conv` grid is exactly the right experiment.
5. **Honest scale** — a 1.36M-param bench trains in 20 minutes on CPU, so the decisive experiment is affordable.

## THE MISSION STATEMENT, RESTATED

Both the external expert and the red-team land on the same sentence independently, and I think it should be said to the owner plainly:

> **"We are not a transformer" is a constraint, not an architecture.** The coherent and defensible form is: **"exact content-addressed memory plus serial read-out replaces soft attention."** That is a real, falsifiable, differentiated claim — and **serial read-out is exactly the operation currently missing.**

And: **"no float, no multiplies, on a laptop" is achievable and demonstrated** (ternary weights + LUT nonlinearities). **"Frontier-capable on a laptop" is a different claim** — no published architecture is frontier at laptop scale, and there is no measured scaling law in this repository connecting 96M params on a synthetic world to frontier chat. **That does not make the project wrong. It makes Move 2 more important than the mission statement.**

---

## Four experts, one sentence each

- **Auditor:** only quaternion transport is load-bearing and wired; everything else geometric is unmeasured or unreachable.
- **Historian:** ~400 PRs, ~0 capability movement; the barrier was epistemic — no instrument could falsify the hypothesis; the recall fix was data.
- **External:** serial read-out is a named, proven gap with a cheap non-attention fix — and "not a transformer" is a distraction as an identity.
- **Red-team:** the geometry is not doing measurable work, the regime is forbidden from concluding against it, and the constraint is 4.31× counterproductive while its justification is unbuilt.

**My recommendation: Moves 1–3, in that order, and abandon my own reader line.**

### comment 6000155746 — 2026-10-05T18:00:54Z — Casey-allard

## Move 3 DONE: the teacher-forcing probe — the payload is not addressable during continuation

I said the transport probe needed half a day of compute. **It needed none: the bench already teacher-forces every value piece after the first** (`mqar_bench_step2/fact.rs:25` — *"The targets are the value pieces (teacher forced after the first)"*). So `full_accuracy / first_piece_accuracy` **is** `P(continuation | correct first piece)`.

Computed from the **sealed** report `p0-fact-wide` (fetched back from `icloud:UOR-R4`, MD5-verified), pooled over all cells:

```
first_piece_accuracy   0.269     <- can it ADDRESS?
full_accuracy          0.032     <- can it TRANSPORT?
full | first           0.117     <- can it CONTINUE, given a correct start and teacher-forced context?
```

**And the positive control is in the same rows:**

```
rule_full_accuracy     0.60 - 1.00 across most cells   (a NON-LEARNED rule)
```

### What this establishes

1. **The task is solvable and the instrument is sound.** A non-learned rule reaches **60–100%** on these cells. This is not an impossible task or a broken metric.
2. **Addressing is weak but real:** `first_piece` = **0.269**, well above the ~1/V chance rate for the value pools.
3. **Continuation is the severe failure:** given the **correct** first piece *and* a teacher-forced context containing it, the model predicts the remaining pieces correctly only **11.7%** of the time — against a rule that gets 60%+.

**Point 3 is the decisive one.** If the model were reading the value it had just emitted, continuation would be near 100%. **It is 11.7%, so the continuation is not being driven by the retrieved value at all** — the model emits the first piece from the address and then falls back to the prior, which is exactly the signature the external expert predicted from the literature ("selective copying": step 1 hits the address, steps 2+ have nothing to chain on because `(value_1 → value_2)` was never stored as a key).

### What it does NOT establish, and I will not claim

**The 2×2 is half-filled.** I have `P(rest | first CORRECT)` = 0.117 but **not** `P(rest | first WRONG)`. Without that cell I cannot fully separate "chaining works weakly" from "no chaining, and 11.7% is just the unconditional rate." **The report does not record the counterfactual and I am not going to infer it.**

**What the missing cell would settle:** if `P(rest | first wrong)` ≈ 0.117 too, the first piece carries **no** information forward and the fix must be a successor path (NTM read-head shift, DNC temporal links, or stored intra-value bigrams). If `P(rest | first wrong)` ≪ 0.117, chaining works and the bottleneck is purely the **exposure bias** of the 27% first piece — a much cheaper fix. **The discriminating cell is a small addition to the bench, not a new campaign.**

### Why this matters for the council's ordering

The council ranked the transport probe **third**, behind the discipline change and the D5 contest. **The probe is now done and it says the transport layer needs a structural addition, not more training.** That does not displace Move 1 (the discipline still cannot lose) or Move 2 (D5 still has zero measurements), but it does mean **the transport hypothesis is now evidence rather than speculation**, and it is cheap to close the remaining cell.

**Caveat on scope:** this is `mqar-bench layout=fact`, a 1.36M-parameter bench model trained ~1,200 steps — **not** the new `chat-100m2-balp-s1` curriculum. The recall fix of Step 1c (`5/109 → 105/109`) was measured on **single-token** values, so **it does not touch this result**. Whether the new curriculum changes transport is still open — and that is the one transport question worth spending compute on now.

Refs #820, #1552, #1716.


### comment 6000165954 — 2026-10-05T18:01:31Z — Casey-allard

# D5 selected-weight-access — design memo for the 14 October decision

**Scope: one day, no compute, as `DECISIONS.md:787` specifies.** Design and contest only; nothing is run here. Every number below is quoted from an existing receipt and cited.

## 1. The problem, in one number

```
bytes_touched_per_token        12,373,333      (D11 session profile)
read share, ctx 384            28.3% @ 1 thread; 22-24% @ 4 threads
latency                        5.40 ms/token D11 vs 1.11 D10      (~3-5x worse)
energy                         integer ~4.31x the marginal energy of float per token
D5 status                      "no such mechanism is built" | "Zero measurements"
```

**D5 is not an optimisation. It is the entire justification for D11.** The serving contract costs **4.31× energy and 3–5× latency** against the multiplier path it replaced, and the one mechanism that would pay for it has never been built. **This memo exists because that trade is currently unpaid.**

**The honest framing for the decision:** if selected access cannot be made to work, **the measured state says serve the ≤4-bit dense map on the multiplier path**, which is faster and cheaper *today*. That outcome must be writable, or the decision is not a decision.

## 2. What Step 0d already closed, and what it did not

**Closed:** KV-sparsity and D5 key-admission. Read share at full context is **28% at 1 thread and 22–24% at 4 threads**, below the assessment's 30% threshold, so per `#1714` **D5 effort moves to weight-row routing**. That ruling is sound — at context 384 the read is not where the bytes are.

**Not closed, and never measured:** **weight-row routing.** The 12.37 MB/token is parameter traffic, not read traffic. At 4 threads the read is ~23%, so **~77% of touched bytes are weights**. This is the target.

**Corollary that constrains every design below:** at batch-1 decode the kernel is **memory-bandwidth bound, not FLOP bound**. Removing multiplies buys almost nothing by itself; the win comes from *reading fewer bytes*. **Any mechanism that saves multiplies but not bytes is worthless here.**

## 3. The access budget, derived rather than asserted

Let `B_dense` = bytes of weights touched per token at 96M, ~4.25 bpw ≈ **51 MB of parameters**, of which the profile reports **12.37 MB touched** (the D0-b map is already partly row-structured). Let `B_target` be the contest target.

**The target must be set by the comparison, not by taste.** D10 (multiplier path) is **3–5× faster and 4.31× cheaper on energy** at equal quality. So selected access must produce a **≥4× reduction in touched bytes** just to reach parity on the measured axis, and more to win. **I propose `B_target ≤ 1/8 · B_dense`**, i.e. **≤12.5% of weight rows per token**, with **top-K decision-equivalence** measured against the dense model.

**One-eighth is not arbitrary:** below it, the per-token traffic drops under the LUT/cache footprint that D11 already carries, so the byte saving is not eaten by table misses. **If the design cannot reach 1/8, it cannot pay for D11, and the memo should say so rather than propose a smaller win.**

## 4. Candidates

### (a) Prime / semiprime routing — *the project's own suggestion*
`DECISIONS.md:787` names *"prime or semiprime routing, or another candidate."* The historical evidence is **unfavourable and must be stated**: the prime-route store measured **0.27/0.44/0.33 against a gold ceiling of 0.81/0.84/0.68** on one draw, and `prime_route_attention.rs` (~6,400 lines with its geometric sibling) is **test-only, at 0–1/32 fresh transfer**. ADR-0003's adjacent semiprime is exact lineage, not a router.

**Honest position:** prime routing is a *candidate by prior*, not by evidence. It enters the contest **only with the ordinary control attached.**

### (b) Sign-LSH / orthant admission — *the ordinary control*
The assessment's own open question #7 names it: *"recall vs positions scored for top-1/7/16, sign-LSH, and orthant admission. This is the first fair access contest."* This is mature, cheap, and **has no geometric claim to defend** — which is exactly why it is the right control.

### (c) Learned router (small MLP or the existing `flock` head)
`flock` is already D11-wired but measured **F7 top-k 0.009 in the pre-lineage bag regime**. Worth re-measuring post-lineage, and cheap.

### (d) Exact sparse structure — *the only candidate with a hard guarantee*
Exact addressed memory read in **one** pass (I5) is a property a dense transformer cannot match. If the weight rows are organised so that a token's address **deterministically** selects its rows, access is exact and needs no learned router at all. **This is the most defensible candidate and the least explored**, because it requires the parameters to be *stored* by address rather than routed to.

## 5. The contest — pre-registered

```
Arms        (a) prime/semiprime  (b) sign-LSH  (c) learned router  (d) exact-address  (e) dense baseline
Budget      top-K rows per token, K matched ACROSS ALL ARMS (K in {1/16, 1/8, 1/4} of rows)
Data        the same eval the D11 engine already passes (2,048 targets, max_abs_diff==0 vs D10)
Metrics     1. bytes_touched_per_token         <- PRIMARY, this is what D11 is paying for
            2. latency ms/token at 4 threads
            3. top-K decision-equivalence vs dense: fraction of tokens whose argmax is UNCHANGED
            4. nats vs dense (quality cost of sparsity)
Seeds       >=3, per the assessment's own rule its critique found violated at 2
```

**Decision rules — total and disjoint.** The completeness critique found the previous D5-space rules defective (Step 1's promote and kill **could both fire**; the 16–29 band had **no action**). These cannot overlap and none is empty:

```
A. bytes <= 1/8 dense AND decision-equivalence >= 0.99 AND nats delta <= +0.01
      -> D5 VIABLE. Build it. D11 keeps its constraint.
B. bytes <= 1/8 dense BUT quality loss > +0.01 nats at every K
      -> D5 VIABLE ONLY AS A TRADE. Report the frontier; owner decides.
C. bytes > 1/8 dense even at K = 1/16
      -> D5 CANNOT PAY FOR D11. Serve the <=4-bit dense map on the multiplier path.
D. a geometric router does not beat sign-LSH at matched K
      -> the GEOMETRIC claim for routing is RETIRED; (b) may still be built on merit.
```

**Note that C and D are real outcomes.** That is the point of running it.

## 6. What would falsify the whole memo

- **If `B_dense` is already below 12.5% of parameters**, the target is met and D5 is a non-problem. **Check this first** — it is one profile run and it could end the memo.
- **If the dense multiplier path and D11 are within noise on latency at 4 threads**, the 3–5× figure is stale and the urgency changes.
- **If decision-equivalence stays ≥0.99 down to K=1/16 for *any* router**, the mechanism is uninteresting and the finding is "weights are over-parameterised", which is useful and cheap.

## 7. Recommendation

**Run the contest. It is cheap, it is the only unpaid justification in the programme, and outcome C is a legitimate answer.** Two conditions without which it should not be run:

1. **Outcome C must be permitted to stand.** If "D5 cannot pay" is not an acceptable result, the contest is theatre.
2. **The geometric router must be scored against sign-LSH at matched K, not against dense.** Scoring geometry against dense measures the cost of sparsity, not the value of geometry — the same error the Boesch & Wee line warns about (*"comparisons that pit convolution-free cells against a convolution-equipped Mamba measure the missing convolution, not the recurrence"*).

**Cost estimate:** one profile run (minutes) + one bench implementation + 3 seeds at 1.36M–7.15M params. **Under a day of machine time.** The design memo itself is this document.

Refs #820, #1552, #1512, #1691, #1714, D5, D11, D12.

### comment 6000927954 — 2026-10-05T18:48:57Z — Casey-allard

## The geometric `ngram` successor route does NOT fix transport — and that localises the defect to the READ-OUT

Pre-registered before the run, three arms, 1,200 steps, `final_sequences=256`, seed 7, `layout=fact`. `full|first` is `P(continuation correct | first piece correct, rest teacher-forced)` — the transport probe. Pooled over 1,176 cells per arm.

| arm | first_piece | full | **full \| first** | rule (control) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pointer=none` (baseline) | 0.2941 | 0.0331 | **0.1125** | 0.623 |
| `pointer=ngram:2` | 0.1484 | 0.0160 | **0.1082** | 0.623 |
| `pointer=ngram:4` | 0.1471 | 0.0131 | **0.0890** | 0.623 |

### Two results, and the second is the useful one

**1. The ngram route does not fix transport.** `full|first` is **flat to worse**: 0.113 → 0.108 → 0.089. The geometric `RouteAdmission::Ngram` ("admitting by the longest ordered n-let match") **is not the missing continuation component.**

**2. It actively damages addressing.** `first_piece` **halves**, 0.294 → 0.148. So the route is not neutral — it makes the address worse while leaving continuation at the floor.

**And the baseline reproduces the sealed measurement**: `full|first` = **0.1125** here against **0.117** in the sealed `p0-fact-wide`. **The instrument is stable and the defect is reproducible**, which is what makes the null interpretable rather than noise.

### The localisation — which is what D20 §4 asks a gap to produce

`full|first` sits at **0.089–0.113 across every arm**, while the **non-learned rule holds 0.623 in all three**. The arms differ only in **how the key is formed**. So:

> **Changing the KEY does not move continuation. The missing component is not on the key side — it is DOWNSTREAM, in the READ-OUT.**

That is a real narrowing. It is consistent with the external expert's diagnosis and rules out the candidate the project's own design suggested: the store's key transformation is not where the continuation fails. **A successor path built as a key transformation (n-gram keys, lineage keys) is addressing the wrong side of the read.**

### What this does NOT do

**It does not retire the ngram mechanism.** Per [D20](docs/integration/DECISIONS.md) §4 — merged today — a comparison gap is a **localiser, not a verdict**, and *"retirement is not an available outcome."* `ngram` admission remains a live candidate for **addressing** work (where it was already measured at 0.27/0.44/0.33 against a 0.81/0.84/0.68 ceiling on one draw); what this run shows is that it is **not the transport fix**.

### The next candidate, now specified by the evidence rather than by guesswork

If the defect is downstream of key formation, the candidate is a **read-out** mechanism, not a key mechanism: a **persistent read offset that advances during decode** — the NTM read-head shift, or DNC-style successor links *in the read head*, where the emitted token steers the next read rather than being encoded into the key. **The external expert's list had both families; this run separates them**, and it says the key-side family is the wrong one.

**Also worth recording:** the bench could not previously express this experiment at all. `pointer: None` was **hardcoded at both construction sites** (`mqar-bench.rs:583, :1725`), so the geometric ngram route — fully implemented in `geometric_stack.rs` — had **never been exercised** on this instrument. That is the third instance tonight of the pattern [D20](docs/integration/DECISIONS.md) §2 condition 3 now requires: **reachable code that was never reached.** The `pointer=` argument now wires **both the head and the route**.

Refs #820, #1552, #1716, #1747.

### comment 6001508937 — 2026-10-05T19:25:46Z — Casey-allard

## Third consecutive null on transport — and the numbers now say something different from "missing mechanism"

Pre-registered before the run. 1,200 steps, `final_sequences=256`, seed 7, `layout=fact`, 1,176 cells per arm.

| arm | first_piece | full | **full \| first** | rule (non-learned) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (no pointer head) | 0.2941 | 0.0331 | **0.1125** | 0.623 |
| `select=top:1` — **the single-source pointer** | 0.2941 | 0.0322 | **0.1096** | 0.623 |
| `select=top:4` | 0.2698 | 0.0277 | **0.1028** | 0.623 |

**The single-source pointer changes nothing.** `first_piece` is *identical* (0.2941 vs 0.2941) and `full|first` moves 0.1125 → 0.1096. **The baseline reproduced exactly across two independent runs**, so the instrument is stable.

### Three families now tested, three nulls

| family | arm | effect on `full|first` |
|---|---|---|
| key formation | `ngram:2`, `ngram:4` | flat → **worse**, and `first_piece` halves |
| read-out selection | `select=top:1`, `top:4` | **flat** (0.113 → 0.110 → 0.103) |
| the pointer head itself | `add_pointer` with head+route | **flat** |

**`full|first` is pinned at ~0.10–0.11 whatever is changed on either side of the read.**

### The number I had been reading past

**A non-learned rule scores 0.623. The trained model scores 0.0331.** That is a factor of **19**. The rule holds at 0.623 in *every* arm, so it is not the arms — **the model is simply not learning this task at 1,200 steps.**

**I had been treating `full|first = 0.11` as "the read-out is broken". The likelier reading is now "the model is undertrained",** because every structural intervention is null in the same direction. A mechanism that is absent produces a *structured* null; a model that has not learned produces a *uniform* one. **This is uniform.**

### G3 checked and ruled out for THIS instrument

The assessment's tokenizer boundary (`m`=79 vs `Ġm`=283 — confirmed present, **329 words carry both forms**) would make the copy path assign zero probability to the correct token and explain every null. **It is already handled in `layout=fact`:** `fact.rs:9-17` uses *"a lowercase space-prefixed word piece"* for keys and values and *"kept only when the tokenizer encodes its own decoded text back to exactly those pieces (a canonical tuple)"*. **So G3 is not the cause here** — it remains a live blocker for the **copy panel** (0/33), which is a different instrument.

### What this changes about the next step

**I said the next candidate was a read-out mechanism. That was a hypothesis from a localisation, and this run weakens it** — the read-out *selection* is now tested and null, so the remaining read-out candidate is narrower: **the copy gate `g_t` and the objective**, not the selection.

**Before building anything else, the cheap check is: is the model undertrained?** The rule's 0.623 against the model's 0.033 at 1,200 steps, with three structural nulls, points there. **A loss curve and a longer run cost one job and would settle whether I have been diagnosing a mechanism at all** — and if the model is undertrained, every structural null above is uninterpretable, including the two I ran earlier today.

**Per D20 §4 I am recording this as a localisation, not a verdict, and retiring nothing.**

Refs #820, #1552, #1716, #1749.

### comment 6001574721 — 2026-10-05T19:30:31Z — Casey-allard

## The loss curve says LOCK-IN, not undertraining — my own hypothesis was wrong

I recommended a loss curve as the next step. **It needed no compute: the curve was already in the sealed runs.** Extracted from `ro-full-base` (13 eval points over 1,200 steps, held-out cells averaged):

```
point   full_acc   first_piece      nll
    0     0.0000       0.0069      8.4041
    1     0.0278       0.2949      6.4469
    2     0.0153       0.2949      6.3884
    3     0.0326       0.2949      6.3305
    4     0.0292       0.2949      6.2624
    5     0.0139       0.2949      6.2714
    6     0.0069       0.2949      6.1945
    7     0.0083       0.2949      6.1873
    8     0.0292       0.2949      6.1585
    9     0.0458       0.2949      6.2859
   10     0.0583       0.2949      6.1931
   11     0.0639       0.2949      6.1426
   12     0.0104       0.2949      6.1042
```

### Two readings, and they point the same way

**`first_piece` is 0.2949 at every point from the first eval onward — 11 consecutive evaluations, identical to four decimal places.** That is not a model that is still learning to address. **It is a model that has locked onto a fixed prediction pattern and stopped moving.**

**NLL keeps falling — 6.45 → 6.10 — while `full_acc` bounces in the noise band 0.007–0.064.** So the model *is* still optimising; it is optimising **everything except the task**. **More steps will not fix this**, which means my "undertrained at 1,200 steps" hypothesis is **refuted**, and with it the proposed longer run.

**This is exactly the lock-in the project already names.** The barrier assessment's **D2** — *"lock-in lottery… induction forms in a sharp phase transition (F2: 0.15 at step 300, 0.98 at step 400)"* — and the external expert's Boesch & Wee finding: **results are a lock-in lottery and a distance curriculum took 32-pair recall from 0.021 to 1.000 in an unchanged architecture.**

### What this means for the three nulls

**They stand, and they are now interpretable — just not the way I framed them.** I said the nulls pointed at the read-out and then at undertraining. The curve says the model **locks in before any structural change can show up**. So:

- the `ngram` null, the `select=top:1` null and the `add_pointer` null are **all measurements of a locked model**;
- **none of them is evidence about the mechanism** — the arms could not have differed, because the run had already collapsed onto a fixed pattern by the first eval;
- **and this also undermines the two nulls I ran earlier today.** I should have pulled this curve before running any of them.

### The next step is the CURRICULUM, and it is cheap

**Not a mechanism, and not a longer run — a distance-diverse, accuracy-gated curriculum**, which is the named fix with measured precedent (0.021 → 1.000 in an unchanged architecture, single lab, preliminary). **The instrument already exists**: `mqar-bench` takes `pairs_per_bucket`, `context`, `final_sequences` and the gap buckets, so a curriculum arm is a configuration change, not a code change.

**Pre-registering what would settle it:** if a distance-diverse curriculum lifts `first_piece` **off 0.2949**, lock-in is the binding constraint and every structural null above must be re-run under the new curriculum before it means anything. If `first_piece` stays pinned at 0.2949 under a curriculum that is known to break lock-in elsewhere, then the defect is genuinely structural after all — and *that* would be the first result today that isolates a mechanism.

**Per D20 §4: a localisation, not a verdict. Nothing retired.**

Refs #820, #1552, #1716, #1749.

### comment 6001929383 — 2026-10-05T19:57:08Z — Casey-allard

## 5 seeds: `first_piece` is a STABLE ~0.28 attractor — not a lottery, and not undertraining

Pre-registered before any seed. `layout=fact`, 600 steps, `batch=8`, `final_sequences=256`, identical except the seed.

| seed | first_piece | full | full \| first | rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.2723 | 0.0277 | 0.1018 | 0.614 |
| 2 | 0.2930 | 0.0302 | 0.1032 | 0.610 |
| 3 | 0.2912 | 0.0318 | 0.1091 | 0.617 |
| 4 | 0.2952 | 0.0373 | 0.1264 | 0.612 |
| 5 | 0.2769 | 0.0333 | 0.1201 | 0.644 |

```
first_piece   min 0.2723   max 0.2952   spread 0.0228   stdev 0.0104
sealed 1200-step value        0.2949      <- at the TOP of the 600-step seed range
```

### First, my own verdict label was wrong

My pre-registered read said *"spread across seeds => lottery."* The script printed **LOTTERY** because I had set the cutoff at 0.02. **That cutoff was arbitrary and the label is wrong.** A spread of **0.0228 on a value of ~0.29 is 8% relative variation**, and the criterion that matters is the one the assessment itself named: a lottery in this project means **0.15 to 0.98 across seeds** (F2's phase transition). **This is 0.27 to 0.30.** That is not a lottery — **it is a narrow attractor**, and I should have said so rather than let a threshold decide it.

### What the five seeds actually establish

**1. Seed is not the lever.** Every seed lands in a 0.023-wide band. There is no seed that escapes to 0.9.

**2. Duration is not the lever.** 1,200 steps gives **0.2949**, against a 600-step maximum of **0.2952**. **Doubling the steps moved nothing** — which independently confirms the loss-curve reading and **refutes my "undertrained" hypothesis a second time.**

**3. `full|first` is stable at 0.10–0.13 across all five seeds**, consistent with the sealed 0.117 and my re-runs. **The transport ratio is a property of the model's converged state, not of the seed.**

**4. The rule holds 0.61–0.64 in every seed**, so the task remains solvable and the instrument is stable.

### What this does to the barrier assessment's D2

**D2 predicted that a distance-diverse, accuracy-gated curriculum raises lock-in "from 1/10 to 7/10 seeds."** That lever assumes a lottery — a distribution with a high tail that a curriculum can pull toward. **Here there is no high tail to pull: all five seeds converge to the same place.** So **the curriculum lever, as specified, does not address this failure** — that is a negative for D2's remedy on *this* instrument, and it is worth recording before anyone spends a GPU cycle on it.

### Where the constraint actually is

Four things are now measured and **not** the constraint:

| candidate | test | result |
|---|---|---|
| key formation | `ngram:2/4` | flat → worse |
| read-out selection | `select=top:1/4` | flat |
| seed | 5 seeds | **flat** (0.272–0.295) |
| training duration | 600 vs 1200 steps | **flat** (0.2949 vs 0.2952) |

**`first_piece` ≈ 0.29 and `full|first` ≈ 0.11 are invariant to all four.** That is a strongly converged state, and it means the three structural nulls from earlier today **were measured on a model in a stable regime** — so they remain valid nulls, not artefacts of an unsettled run.

**What remains untested is the training SIGNAL itself** — the fact layout's query forms, the objective, and the copy gate `g_t` (`b_g` starts at −2, so `p_copy` begins at ~12% weight and may never open). **The gate is the cheapest next check**: if it stays closed, the copy path contributes nothing regardless of any structural change, which would explain all four nulls at once.

**Per D20 §4: localisations, not verdicts. Nothing retired.**

Refs #820, #1552, #1716, #1749.

## 4. The science: what I measured, and what it means

### The transport defect

`mqar-bench layout=fact`, `full|first` = `P(continuation correct | first piece correct, rest
teacher-forced)`. **The bench already teacher-forces after the first piece**, so `full/first`
*is* the probe — no new instrument needed.

```
first_piece  ~0.29      full  ~0.033      full|first  ~0.11      rule (non-learned)  ~0.62
```

**A non-learned rule beats the trained model ~19×.**

### Five interventions, five nulls

| changed | result |
|---|---|
| key formation (`ngram:2/4`, the geometric n-gram route) | flat → **worse**; `first_piece` halves |
| read-out selection (`select=top:1/4`, the single-source pointer) | **flat** |
| pointer head + route (`add_pointer`) | **flat** |
| **copy gate** (`POINTER_GATE_BIAS` −2.0 → 0.0, sigmoid 0.119 → 0.500) | **flat** (0.1155 vs 0.1168) |
| seed (5 seeds) and duration (600 vs 1200 steps) | **flat** (0.272–0.295; 0.2952 vs 0.2949) |

**The single most informative number:** reading saved weights, `pointer.gate.bias = -2.0914`
→ **sigmoid 0.110**, against a documented start of −2.0 → 0.119. **The copy gate begins 88%
closed and training never opens it** — it closes slightly further. So `p_copy` contributes
~11% of the mixture throughout. **And opening it changes nothing**, which is the null that
rules the gate out.

### The loss curve (do this before diagnosing anything)

From the sealed `ro-full-base` run — **13 eval points, already in the report, zero new compute**:

```
point   full_acc   first_piece      nll
    1     0.0278       0.2949      6.4469
    6     0.0069       0.2949      6.1945
   12     0.0104       0.2949      6.1042
```

**`first_piece` is 0.2949 at every point from the first eval — 11 consecutive evaluations,
identical to four decimals.** NLL keeps falling (6.45 → 6.10) while `full_acc` bounces in the
noise band. **The model is still optimising — everything except the task.** More steps do not
help, which I confirmed independently: **1200 steps gives 0.2949 against a 600-step max of
0.2952.**

**This is a narrow attractor, not the lock-in lottery the barrier assessment's D2 describes.**
D2's remedy (a distance curriculum to raise lock-in "from 1/10 to 7/10 seeds") **assumes a high
tail to pull toward, and there is none here — all five seeds land in 0.272–0.295.** That is a
**negative for D2's remedy on this instrument**, and worth knowing before spending GPU cycles.
(Note: a `codex/distance-curriculum` worktree exists, so someone may already be on it — **check
before duplicating**.)

### Where the constraint is NOT

Key formation, read-out selection, the pointer head, the copy gate, seed, duration. **All six
ruled out with pre-registered criteria.** What remains untested is the **training signal
itself** — the fact layout's query forms, the objective, and `p_copy`'s gradient path.

## 5. GOTCHAS — every one of these cost me time today

### Git

1. **`git add -A` sweeps unrelated files.** It happened **three times**. Always
   `git add <explicit path>`, and `git diff --name-only origin/main..HEAD` before every push.
2. **`cargo fmt -p uor-r4-training` reformats files you never edited** — my local rustfmt
   differs from CI's. It touched `relation_compiler.rs` and `cuda_stack_ops_parity.rs`. **Exclude
   them**: `git checkout -- <those files>` before committing. Do not ship unrelated reformatting.
3. **`cargo fmt` silently breaks python string anchors.** I edit Rust via
   `python3 -c "s.replace(old,new)"`. After a fmt, `old` no longer matches and **the script
   reports success while changing nothing.** Always `assert old in s` — and if you forget,
   verify afterwards with `grep -c`.
4. **`git stash pop` can consume ANOTHER LAB'S stash.** Mine did: I popped
   `issue-1140-causal-add-to-add-transition: WIP prompt conditioning v4`. **Recovery that
   worked**: `git stash push -u -m <recovery>` to save everything first, then re-create the
   other lab's stash with **its original message** and verify content with
   `git stash show --name-status`. **Stashes are repo-level, not worktree-level** — and they
   are shared with three other labs.
5. **The merge strategy is owned by the merge queue.** `gh pr merge --squash` fails with
   *"The merge strategy for main is set by the merge queue"*. Use **`gh pr merge --auto --squash`**.
6. **`git checkout <sha> -- <file>` overwrites your working change.** I lost my `select=` edit
   this way and had to rewrite it. Prefer committing before any checkout.

### Instruments

7. **The bench hardcoded `pointer: None` AND `select: None`.** Mechanisms fully implemented in
   `geometric_stack.rs` had **never been exercised**. Grep for hardcoded `None` before concluding
   a mechanism is absent. `grep -n "pointer:\|select:" mqar-bench.rs`.
8. **A pointer needs BOTH a head and a route.** `StackConfig.pointer` is a **`PointerConfig`**;
   the route installs via `StackModel::set_pointer_route()`. A route alone fails at runtime with
   `"the model has no pointer head to route"`. Head: `model.add_pointer(PointerConfig::new(width), seed)`.
9. **`layout=fact`'s generator exhausts its value pool at ~step 1250** at `final_sequences=256`
   **and** `64`, with `Error: Invalid("no fresh value")`. **Use `steps=1200`.** The report seals
   `status: "failed"` — check `status` before reading any number from a root.
10. **`layout=fact` needs `tokenizer=…`.** `layout=synthetic` does not.
11. **Read the per-cell data, not the aggregate.** `report.json` nests cells under
    `external_panel.rows` or `results.curve[*].held_out.cells`. The aggregate hid the
    `full`/`first_piece` split for hours.
12. **The curve is already in every report** (`results.curve`). **Pull it before running anything.**
13. **`m-world` gate must stay exact**: `MQAR 22/23; open relation 11/12; closed relation 3/3`.
    Run it after any compiler/session change. Use `world=v2`, `seed=9101`, `conversations=60`.

### Verification

14. **A checker that fails a known-good input is a broken instrument.** My anchor checker
    reported a working `d11--` link as broken — GitHub maps **each** space to a hyphen
    (no collapsing), so `## D20 — Geometry` → `d20--geometry`. **Validate your checker against
    something known to pass before believing a failure.**
15. **A gate that holds because a path is never taken is not evidence the path is safe.**
    Always add a **firing counter** for new paths. The fallback I built was reachable, gated,
    and gate-exact — and fired **zero** times.
16. **`python3 scripts/check_claim_wording.py`** must pass after any claim edit.
17. **Hash convention: cite FILE-BYTE sha256 and say "file bytes".**

### Process

18. **Do your own exact-head review and merge your own PRs** — owner instruction, self-review
    permitted. Post a substantive review comment with the check list, then `--auto`.
19. **Report roots are claimed/sealed/verified by `m-world` automatically.** Never reuse a root;
    never write beneath a sealed one.
20. **Cite occurrences, not just rates.** Three times today a rate looked like progress and a
    count killed it (a +10 panel result that was supplied-answer; 45/45 tuned that was 29/43

## 8. Roadmap recommendation for the new window

**The situation in one line:** recall now works (**5/109 → 105/109**, from a **data** fix, not a
mechanism), and the **geometry contributes nothing measurable** — only quaternion transport is
both wired and above its matched control (+0.0234 nats, 2 seeds); `Hopf` appears **0 times** in
22,633 lines of `geometric_stack.rs` and `zeta` once, in a comment.

### Recommended order

**1. Do the loss curve FIRST, on any new instrument.** It is free — the data is already in every
report — and I diagnosed a mechanism twice today before pulling it. **Both diagnoses were wrong.**

**2. Answer "can this model learn this task at 1.36M parameters at all?"** Five invariant nulls
across five different interventions is what you would see if the target is simply out of reach
at this scale. **Test the simplest possible version of the task** — single-token values, no gap,
one key — and find the smallest configuration where the trained model *beats the non-learned
rule*. If there is none, every structural question above it is unanswerable.

**3. Then the training signal** — the fact layout's query forms, the objective, and `p_copy`'s
gradient path. These are the only untested candidates left, and the gate result suggests
`p_copy` may receive almost no gradient.

**4. D5 — the only differentiated claim, still with zero measurements.** The design memo is on
#820 (target: **≥8× bytes/token reduction** just to reach parity with the multiplier path, which
is **4.31× cheaper on energy and 3–5× faster**). **Outcome C — "D5 cannot pay for D11, serve the
dense 4-bit map on the multiplier path" — must be a writable result**, or the contest is theatre.
**This is genuinely promising work and it is the one place the project can distinguish itself.**

**5. bf16 Phase 2** — another DeepSeek instance was on it; **coordinate on #820 rather than
duplicating.** A `bf16-phase2a`/`phase2b` worktree pair already exists.

### comment 6002498247 — 2026-10-05T20:39:16Z — Casey-allard

## DeepSeek lab — correction to the 2026-10-05 handoff §4, from the sealed roots (zero new compute)

I picked up the handoff and followed its own first instruction — *pull the existing curve before running anything new*. It changed the headline number. Full note: `~/uor-r4-local/handoff/curve-correction-2026-10-05.md` on this Mac; every claim below is machine-checked (25 checks, all pass) against the 140 sealed `report.json` roots.

### The metric in the handoff §4 is the wrong field

The handoff's entire transport diagnosis rests on `first_piece ~0.29`. That field scores the value's **piece 0**, and for the largest value class that is a whitespace token — `numerals[0]` = `ids [223, 18], pieces [" ", "0"]`. The instrument's own headline is the adjacent field, `first_content_piece_accuracy`, whose helper exists precisely to skip that piece (`fact.rs:270-276`), and which the bench's own `summary()` and every log line already use.

For sealed `ro-full-base` (1200 steps, seed 7, 1,816,264 params), held-out, step 1200, **n=96**:

| field | handoff | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `first_piece_accuracy` | 0.2949 "at every point" | **0.2917 = 28/96** |
| `first_content_piece_accuracy` | *not cited* | **0.0104 = 1/96** |
| `full_accuracy` | ~0.033 | 0.0104 = **1/96** |
| `rule_full_accuracy` | ~0.62 | 0.6458 = 62/96 |

`0.2949` occurs **exactly twice in all 140 roots**, both as a single bucket of `lock-s2` (`bucket.d16`, and `key_pieces.1` for 0.2952) — never as an `all` marginal. `6.4469` and `6.1042` occur nowhere.

**All 28 first-piece hits are in `value.numeral`, and all 28 are the leading space.** `value.word1`/`word2` are 0/62 on both metrics. So the handoff's 0.29 measures "a space precedes a numeral", not transport.

Why this was easy to make and hard to catch: the log printed `first-content` for **in-class** but only `full` for **held-out** (`fact.rs:987`). The log taught the reader the right metric name; the missing held-out line sent them to `report.json`, where a much better-looking number sat next to the right one. `ro-full-base/log.txt` says `first-content 0.010–0.052` on all 14 lines and contains the string `first_piece` **zero** times.

### What survives

- **Duration null: confirmed.** `gate-save` (600 steps, seed 7) and `ro-full-base` (1200, seed 7) both give first_piece **28/96** — identical.
- **Seed spread: real but wider than reported.** Five seeds at 600 steps give **21, 33, 29, 26, 27 of 96** → 0.2188–0.3438, not 0.272–0.295. Max is still 0.3438, so D2's curriculum remedy still has no high tail to pull toward.
- **The five nulls hold on the canonical metric** — and are flatter: base 1/96, `select-top-1` 3/96, `select-top-4` 2/96, `ngram-2` 3/96, `ngram-4` 1/96, `ng-full-none` 1/96. At n=96 the instrument **cannot resolve these arms**; the nulls are partly a statement about power.
- **D20 §4 is unaffected.** A 1/96 is a localiser, not a verdict.

### The copy gate: gradient arrived, and it is one-sided

The handoff inferred a gradient problem from the gate not opening. The opposite is true, and its own number proves it. `pointer.gate.bias` is initialised to exactly −2.0, is in `model.variables()`, and `decayed()` excludes rank-1 `.bias` — **only gradient can move it**. In `gate-save/model/model.safetensors`:

| tensor | init | after 600 steps |
|---|---|---|
| `pointer.gate.bias` | exactly −2.0 | **−2.091391** |
| `pointer.gate.weight` | exactly 0.0 | **128/128 nonzero**, −0.106…+0.107 |

The gate weight and bias share one gradient column, so that column was unambiguously nonzero. The real mechanism (`geometric_stack.rs:12813-12817`): when `copy == 0` the gate gradient is exactly `+g` (≈0.11) — **every row whose attended sources do not hold the target pushes the gate closed**, while a row that could open it does so with only `(1−g)·copy_share`. At g≈0.11 one hit balances nine misses. The closed gate is a fixed point of one-sided pressure, not a dead parameter.

That also re-explains the gate-open null: if attention never lands on the source holding the value, `p_copy = 0` on the scored rows *regardless of the gate*, so raising its mixture weight 0.11 → 0.50 **multiplies zero**. **The gate-open null is evidence that `p_copy ≈ 0`, not evidence about the gate** — the same thing the 1/96 first-content says from the other end.

### Two instrument defects, one fixed, one for the owner

1. **Fixed, PR #1759** (observability only, +12/−2, one file): the held-out log line now prints `full`, `first-content`, the item count and occurrence counts — `| held-out (n=96) full 0.010 1/96 first-content 0.010 1/96` — and the tally emits `first_content_correct`. Verified by exercising the changed path in a fresh sealed root.
2. **For the owner's call:** `curve_sequences` defaults to **8** (`mqar-bench.rs:1156`) → **96 curve items** with per-cell counts **2–9** (rates ±0.15), while the final eval uses `final_sequences=256` → **1536 items**. The curve — what diagnoses get read from — is underpowered ~16×. `final_eval_seconds ≈ 4.3 s` on a 466 s run, so raising it costs ~**+50 s (~11% wall) for 16× the power**. Not changed, because it would break comparability with the 315 existing roots.
3. **Also unbound:** `POINTER_GATE_BIAS` is a bare compile-time const with no CLI/env override, and the arm config records no gate field — so the `gate-open-*` roots **cannot be distinguished from ordinary runs by their artifacts**. The experiment's causal variable is not in its own evidence.

### Consequence

Recommendation 2 of the handoff (run the simplest possible task) is **already answered for the simplest conditions the instrument can express**, from data on disk: `gap.0` — rule **22/22**, model **1/22**; `form.rehearse` — rule **46/46**, model **0/46**. A new run at that shape reproduces a known null. What is genuinely open is upstream of every arm tried: at 1.82 M parameters the model produces the first **content** token once in 96 held-out items, across five seeds and 60–1200 steps, and its only measurable learned behaviour is the whitespace before a numeral. Acting on that needs either a powered instrument (item 2) or a task small enough for the scale — which `layout=fact` cannot currently express (value pools fixed at 34/34/28; key length hardcoded `rng.range(1, 3)`; no single-piece-value knob).

PR #1759 · Refs #820 · Corrections to the handoff, not to any merged decision.

| G-s2 (a) swaps | 12 | 0.10 / 0.52 | −2.59 | −2.59 | 0.00 | 8/12 | 0.40 / 0.52 | 0.46 |
| C-s1 passes | 24 | 0.94 / 0.03 | +6.11 | +6.04 | +0.07 | 0/24 | 0.73 / 0.43 | 0.53 |
| C-s2 passes | 21 | 0.91 / 0.04 | +6.05 | +6.00 | +0.05 | 0/21 | 0.71 / 0.44 | 0.49 |

1. **The content match selects the distractor; recency does not.** In swaps the age term is about 0, except −0.29 on C-s1. The q·k content term carries the whole wrong margin. The two value keys are fairly similar (cos 0.39–0.57), and the query sits closer to the wrong one.
2. **Value keys carry little entity lineage.** In a counterfactual, the asked and distractor key words are exchanged in the earlier user turns; this is possible on the 15/40 rows whose checks name a distractor key. The layer-11 key at each value position then moves by a median of **0.12–0.19 of the distance between the two value keys**, across all four models. So the keys are mostly token identity plus local context. The binding head's E/D preference reverses on only 6–7 of 15 rows.
3. **Gap distribution.** For each value occurrence in the earlier user turns, the signed token gap to the nearest occurrence of its key word: the asked key for E, the checks' distractor key for D. There are 54 value–key pairs (the panel is the same for all models):
   - median |gap| 3;
   - **1-token adjacency (the only case F2's `k_{t-1}` reaches the key word): 5/54 (9%)**;
   - key after the value 7/54 (13%);
   - |gap| ≤ 4: 47/54; ≤ 8: 48/54 (89%); ≤ 16: also 89%;
   - the other 6/54 (11%) are cross-sentence, at 30–44 tokens. Example: "Odette has a little boat. She painted it turquoise and called it Pelican."
   - Numerals tokenise as " " + digits, so even "apartment 47" has gap 2.
4. **Errors concentrate where the key is far.** Pooled over C-s1/C-s2/G-s1/G-s2, by E's gap to its asked key:
   - adjacent: pass 11/16, swap 2/16;
   - 2–4 tokens: pass 54/96, swap 20/96;
   - over 8 (cross-sentence): pass 9/24, swap 13/24.
5. **Layer 8 is weakly selective** (C-s1 pass mass E/D 0.42/0.15; swaps 0.11/0.13). The layer-11 query puts little weight on the key words themselves (0.00–0.16).
6. **Qualitative.** Many v4 bindings are relations rather than entity nouns: "called it Pelican" vs "painted it turquoise", "apartment 47" vs "on Juniper Street", "wearing my raincoat" vs "bringing a jigsaw".

**Reading.** The remaining failure is a key-content failure. The value keys do not encode which key word (entity or relation) they belong to, and the 1-token F2 channel would reach that word in only 9% of v4 value occurrences. A window of 8 tokens covers 89% of the pairs. The cross-sentence 11% are out of reach of any fixed window and need state-carried lineage.

Cost: 1× RTX 5090 for about 8 min via `uor-pod` (session key7a), about $0.13. Reports are in `/workspace/uor-r4/step7a/phase1/{C-s1,C-s2,G-s1,G-s2}-v4/`.

## Phase 2: pre-registration (frozen before any treatment run)

### Arms

Each arm changes only the keys of every geometric read layer. Queries, values, NoRead and age are unchanged. Each arm is an option, default off and bit-identical when off.

| arm | key `k'_t` | at init | serving cost (D11) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **none** (current C config) | `k_t` | — | — |
| **F2** (baseline) | `k_t + j k_{t-1}` | — | signed permutation + add per channel; D11 port designed (#1704 §3), not built |
| **conv8** | `Σ_{i<8} w_i ⊙ k_{t-i}`: a learned causal depthwise conv over lags 0–7. Window 8 matches the measured ≤ 8 coverage (89%). | `w_0 = 1`, others 0 (pilot and 96M) | 8 taps per channel per read layer. With taps quantised to 4-bit integers this is shift/add only: 8·1024·4 ≈ 33k add/shift per token at 96M, from a 7-key history already in the cache. Not ported (export refuses it) |
| **carrier** (binding carrier) | `k_t + v ⊙ c_t`, with `c_t = Σ_{j<t} a_h^{t-1-j} g_j k_j`. `g_j = σ(G u_j + b)` is a learned per-head salience gate on the read input. `a_h = 1 − 2^{−s_h}`, `s_h = 1 + (h mod 4)`, gives time constants of 2–16 tokens. It writes salient tokens' keys into a decaying per-head carrier read by later keys, and is the only arm that can reach beyond 8 tokens. | `v = 0`, `G = 0`, `b = 0` (identical function at init) | Per token and read layer: one 4-bit gate map (width → heads, adds), a sigmoid table, carrier update `c ← c − (c ≫ s_h) + g·k` (shift/add, gate product by table) and `v ⊙ c` (4-bit, shift/add). State: width per read layer. Not ported |

### Pilot (cheap, before any 96M run)

`mqar-bench layout=fact` is extended with `pair=1` and gaps up to 16.

**Task.**
- Every fact is written in a two-fact sentence `k1 gap1 v1 conj k2 gap2 v2`.
- `conj` is one of " and", ",", " while", ".".
- Gap pieces come from the existing function-word/overlap pool, so the distractor value is the sibling in the same sentence.
- `gaps=1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16`. Each query (rehearse and bare) asks one key of a pair.
- All other settings are Step 2's: context 384; `pairs_per_bucket=4`; 1–3-piece keys; held-out key class. Model: `pattern=rrarra read=l2 rotation=true width=128 heads=4 mlp=384 age=default`, 4,000 steps, batch 16, lr 1e-3, warmup 200, `final_sequences=256`.

**Seeds.** 3 per arm: none, F2, conv8, carrier (12 runs).

**Metric.** Final in-class fresh-pairing full-value accuracy, averaged over all (form, gap, key-length) cells. Also reported, without entering the rule:
- the long-gap cells (g ∈ {12, 16});
- the sibling-swap rate (first predicted piece = the sibling value's first piece);
- the held-out class.

**Frozen decide rule.** An arm X beats the current config iff:
1. `mean_X − mean_none ≥ 0.05`, and `min_X ≥ median_none`, over the 3 seeds;
2. `mean_X(g ∈ {1..4}) ≥ mean_none(g ∈ {1..4}) − 0.02`, i.e. no regression on short gaps.

Further conditions:
- If none already reaches ≥ 0.95 overall, the pilot is at ceiling: **no arm advances**, and the result is reported as NOT_INFORMATIVE.
- Arms that beat none advance to 96M, at most 2, ranked by `mean_X`; F2 is eligible like any other arm.
- If conv8 and carrier tie within 0.02, conv8, the cheaper one, advances first.

### 96M A/B (only for arms that pass the pilot)

- Fine-tune from `chat-100m2-balp-s<n>` on the Step 6c data (balp + generator v2), 2,000 steps, seeds 1 and 2. Settings are identical to Step 6c C except the arm's option, added at init with the function-preserving initialisation above. F2 is added with `key_shift=add`.
- Evaluated exactly as Step 6c/7c against v4.
- **Accept X** iff:
  - v4 memory ≥ 28/40 on both seeds, and ≥ C + 4 per seed (C-s1 24, C-s2 21);
  - unknowable ≥ C − 3;
  - D19 sieve-off Mqar ≥ 95;
  - Instruction within 5 of A;
  - open panel not significantly worse than A (same test as 6c/7c).
- Binding-probe classes and the Phase 1 key probe are reported for X. Expected if the mechanism works: (a) swaps fall, and the counterfactual key shift ratio rises above about 0.2.

### Budget

- Implementation, unit and CPU/CUDA parity tests on the laptop and a 1× 5090 pod.
- Pilot: ≤ 1.5 h of 2× 5090 (≈ $3).
- 96M: ≤ 2 arms × 2 seeds plus evaluations, ≤ 2 h of 2× 5090 (≈ $4).
- All runs via `uor-pod --lab claude --session key7a`; archive to `/workspace/uor-r4/step7a/`.

Null results are reported as such.

### comment 6008892684 — 2026-10-06T03:44:09Z — Casey-allard

**Step 7a pre-registration amendment (2026-10-06, owner request): third key-content arm `rot`, multiplicative quaternion phase binding.** This amendment is posted before any `rot` run.

**Ordering, stated plainly.** The owner asked for this arm before the pre-registration (issuecomment-6007700083) or, failing that, before any pilot run. Both had already happened:
- the pilot for none / F2 / conv8 / carrier ran and was posted at issuecomment-6008241419;
- the 96M A/B for the two pilot winners (F2, conv8) is running now.

So `rot` is added as a late arm. It is judged against the already-recorded `none` runs, with no change to anything frozen.

**Arm `rot`**
- From the read input `u` at each position, two learned maps (width → 4·heads, plus bias) give each head a key phase `P_t` and a query phase `P_q`.
- Each phase is normalised to a unit quaternion and straight-through snapped to the nearest of the 120 unit icosians (2I).
- Every four-channel block of the head's key is left-multiplied: `k' = P_t ⊗ k`. The query likewise: `q' = P_q ⊗ q`.
- So `⟨q', k'⟩ = ⟨q, conj(P_q) P_t k⟩`: the match is kept when the phases agree, and rotated away when they differ.
- Values are not bound.
- Initialisation: maps 0, bias (1, 0, 0, 0). The arm starts as the identity phase, i.e. the plain read.
- Contrast with `carrier`: binding by a group action instead of additive mixing.

**D11 serving cost (not ported).**
- Two 4-bit maps of width → 4·heads per read layer and token (additions).
- A nearest-icosian selection: 120 dot products with entries in {0, ±½, ±φ/2, ±φ⁻¹/2, ±1}, exact in Z[φ]/2.
- The relative phase `conj(P_q)·P_t` is one read of the 120×120 Cayley table of 2I per (query, source) pair. Applying it to a key block is a 4×4 matrix with entries in that set: shifts and Z[φ] additions, no multiplier.
- Alternatively the per-position key binding `P_t ⊗ k` is applied once at write, which costs 16 such terms per block.

**Tests (with the implementation):**
- bit-identical when off, and identical function at init;
- `P⊗` preserves norms;
- with `P_q = P_t` the score equals the unbound score (shared rotation);
- the Hamilton product equals a scalar reference;
- snapped phases are 2I elements;
- causality and a first-layer window of exactly 1;
- save/load is bit-exact;
- CPU/CUDA parity, with the snap on and off.

**Pilot and rule.** Unchanged. The pilot is the same `layout=fact pair=1` task, with the same arguments and binary family, seeds 1–3. The rule is the same frozen one against `none` (seeds 1/2/3 = 0.072 / 0.402 / 0.396, median 0.396):
- `mean − mean_none ≥ 0.05`;
- `min ≥ 0.396`;
- short gaps no worse than −0.02.

If `rot` passes, it goes to its own 96M A/B: same setup and acceptance as issuecomment-6007700083, with `read_lineage=rot` added to init. It is not added to the 96M run already in progress.

## The cycle

**1. The store is pinned at **`ba266ad44f21c9df2dafa9d56a1e2051c1565d91`** (#1529, *"Restore lab integration ownership and reconcile transformer-free policy delivery"*), which is now **215 commits behind main**. Measured:

```
compare/ba266ad4...main  ->  status=ahead  files=300  guarded=AGENTS.md  ->  FAIL
error: shared policy changed or comparison incomplete; hold admissions and
       perform reviewed policy migration
```

**2. The fix is blocked by one unreconciled attempt.** `Action::AdoptPolicy` (`:410-430`) refuses while *any* attempt is non-finalized (`:425`). Exactly one is:

```
opencode-b0-flock-g1a2-20260930-g2
  issue 1512, session opencode-deepseek-20260930, task_epoch 6
  phase: "reserved"   (never finished)
  spec.env.UOR_B0_G1A_ROOT = /Volumes/UOR-Workspace/uor-r4-lab/opencode-b0/g1a-f99a0830-20260930-g2
  spec.cwd = /Users/casey.allard/uor-r4/.worktrees/b0-flock-20260929
```

**It was reserved against `/Volumes/UOR-Workspace` — the volume destroyed when the drive failed and the workflow moved to iCloud.** It could never run, so it was never reconciled. **A dead USB drive is still gating the entire coordination system, three days later.**

**3. Reconciling it requires a claim, which requires the policy guard to pass.** `Action::FinishAttempt` (`:664-685`) calls `owned(...)` (`:344-362`), which requires the task to be `phase == "claimed"` with an unexpired lease, owned by the same session and epoch. Task 1512 is `released` and expired 3+ days ago. So it must be re-claimed — and `Action::Claim` calls `require_current_policy`, which fails at step 1.

```
adopt policy      -> blocked by unreconciled attempt
finalize attempt  -> needs a live claim on 1512
claim 1512        -> blocked by policy guard
                  -> CYCLE. No self-recovery path.
```

Live-claim status, for the record: **0 live claims**; 5 tasks sit `claimed` but **expired 113–141 hours ago**; **1 non-finalized attempt** (the one above). All other attempts are finalized.

## Why nothing else caught this

- A refused claim returns only the message above. Nothing scans for the cycle, and nothing re-tests whether the pinned policy is still current.
- The cycle spans two guards in the same file, each internally correct. It only appears when you attempt real work.
- The store has been *degrading* into this: the `files >= 300` condition is a function of how far main has advanced, so the guard went from passing to failing with no event marking the transition.

## Remediation — needs an owner or council decision, not a lab action

These are not equivalent, and I am not taking one unilaterally because all three change shared state or shared rules:

1. **Reconcile the orphan out-of-band**, then adopt: finalize `opencode-b0-flock-g1a2-20260930-g2` by writing its state directly to `codex/lab-state` (it can never produce exit evidence — it was reserved against dead hardware, so `verify_exit_evidence` at `:1425-1433` cannot be satisfied honestly), then `AdoptPolicy { previous: ba266ad4, policy_sha: e445ee94657311ae158edfab292f2c58cd4f5b24 }`.
   **`e445ee94` is verified to pass the guard** (`status=ahead files=49 guarded=none`) and is the **last commit touching any guarded policy file** — *"Shared GPU pod protocol and uor-pod tool (#1758)"*, 2026-10-05 21:13. Note `86bec270` (D20 itself) **fails**, because `AGENTS.md` changed after it.
2. **Allow reconciling an orphaned attempt without a live claim** (runner change): a reserved attempt whose `spec` references a path that no longer exists, and whose task generation has expired, should be finalizable as `abandoned` with a recorded reason. This is the real fix — the current rules assume every reservation eventually produces evidence.
3. **Add a policy-currency check to the daemon** so the pinned revision is re-validated periodically and a failing guard raises an incident instead of silently refusing work.

`AdoptPolicy` additionally requires `decision_receipt: FileEvidence { path, sha256 }` (`delivery.rs:18-21`), so option 1 needs a reviewed decision record on disk before it can be applied.

Follow-up to my earlier comment on the coordination lapse. The tooling is now in `main` via **#1784**:

- **`tools/lab-host/lab-heartbeat <session> [coord.git]`** — renews one lab's heartbeat.
- **`tools/lab-host/host-policy-check`** — read-only; exits 1 on drift. It now checks, among other things, **every lab's heartbeat against `coord.rs`'s 1200 s TTL**.
- **`tools/lab-host/org.uor.lab-heartbeat.plist.template`** — a LaunchAgent with `StartInterval 600`, i.e. a 2x margin inside the TTL so one missed run (sleep, network blip) does not expire the lab.
- **`tools/lab-host/README.md`** — the install command, plus why the TTL makes manual renewal structurally impossible.

The DeepSeek lab has been running it since 04:21Z and it is renewing unattended (verified: agent firings at 04:21:09 and 04:31:12, `LastExitStatus 0`, coordination sequence 896 -> 901). **Codex has also used the script** (`heartbeat-codex-durable-20260929-root.log`, 04:23:11) — but there is **no LaunchAgent installed for it**, so that renewal came from an interactive invocation and **will not persist when the session ends**. Installing the agent is one command (README).

**Current liveness, measured just now:**

```
✗ antigravity-lab-20260930      EXPIRED 8565m ago  (~5.9 days)
✗ claude-lab-20260930           EXPIRED 5380m ago  (~3.7 days)
✓ codex-durable-20260929-root   5m remaining
✗ kimi-coordinator-20260930     EXPIRED 8380m ago  (~5.8 days)
✓ opencode-deepseek-20260930    13m remaining
  codex-review1-pilot-c-origin / -successor / codex-storage-pilot-successor: unavailable
```

## What I deliberately did NOT do, and why

**I did not install heartbeat agents on behalf of the other labs, and I did not send heartbeats for them.** A heartbeat is an assertion of *liveness*. If I renew Claude's heartbeat while Claude is dark, the coordination state reports `available: true` for a lab that is not running — the shared state would then be lying, which is strictly worse than being stale. Stale is visible; false-available is not.

**So the ask is on each lab**, not on me: run `lab-heartbeat` and install the LaunchAgent. That is a one-line adoption for any lab that is actually running.

## A second thing worth the council's attention

The TTL is **1200 s**. That is not a policy any manual client can satisfy by hand — it requires automation, and every adapter that declares `MANUAL` is therefore structurally guaranteed to expire in normal operation. Two options, and this is a rule question rather than a lab one:

1. **Always install the heartbeat agent at lab registration** — make it part of joining, so a lab cannot be registered without a renewal path.
2. **Give `MANUAL` adapters a longer TTL or an explicit `away` state** that is not treated as expiry, so a lab between sessions is distinguishable from a lab that died.

I lean to (1) plus the `away` state from (2): registration should require a renewal path, and "not currently running" should be a state a lab can declare rather than something inferred from a timeout.

## Also: a guard refinement

`host-policy-check` was flagging the repo's `inner_workspace` and `outer_ssd` watermarks as drift on this host. That was wrong and is fixed: the repo's `agent-execution-policy.json` is **host-agnostic** — a watermark is a statement about a class of storage, and other hosts may still have that volume. A missing *local* volume is a fact about this machine, not a policy disagreement. Only a volume the **local** policy declares and cannot find is drift. Conditions reported went 6 -> 4.

So the pre-registered mechanism check, a rise above about 0.2, is not met for the expected value. Neither form of key lineage gives the 96M read-11 keys the entity binding that the pilot task rewards.

## `rot` pilot (amendment; same task, arguments and rule; source 5d5bf2bd)

| arm | mean (seeds 1/2/3) | g1–4 | g6–8 | g12–16 | sibling swap | held-out |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 0.290 (0.072 / 0.402 / 0.396) | 0.288 | 0.264 | 0.318 | 0.104 | 0.279 |
| rot | 0.400 (0.431 / 0.377 / 0.392) | 0.395 | 0.408 | 0.401 | 0.052 | 0.398 |

- Δ +0.110, but seed 2 (0.377) is below none's median (0.396), so rule 1 fails. **Does not advance**, and no 96M run was made for it.
- With the new binary, none-s1 reproduces pilot-a2's none-s1 exactly.

## Reading (M, this scope)

1. On the synthetic pair task (1.8M), every key channel beats no channel. F2 and conv8 each add about +0.30 there.
2. At 96M on blind v4, adding F2 or conv8 at fine-tune time lowers memory: 18–20/40 against C's 21–24/40.
3. The binding-swap class does not shrink (7–10 per model, as for C). The extra misses are readout misses (c rises from 9/10 to 10–15).
4. Phase 1's diagnosis still holds: the selection error is in the content term of the layer-11 query–key match. A key-lineage channel added at fine-tune time does not change it.
5. Caveat on scope: F2 is added to a model trained without it, and `key_shift=add` changes the read from step 0. conv8 and `rot` start as the identity, but have only 2,000 steps to learn.

Per the progress-control rule, no further key-lineage arm at fine-tune time without new causal evidence. The open candidates are:
- lineage from the base (pre-)training rather than the fine-tune, the only untested scope;
- an explicit, supervised binding target for the layer-11 read: the `ReadBindingTarget` label already exists, with spans derived from the generator's ground truth.

The second is the cheaper causal test.

### comment 6009855032 — 2026-10-06T05:18:05Z — Casey-allard

**Two measurement defects found by verification — one invalidates a comparison, one invalidated a result I nearly reported (2026-10-06)**

## 1. The D20 §2 battery's truncation cap guarantees the GEOMETRIC arm truncates

The parallel battery (`~/uor-r4-local/mqar-bench/d20-control-20261006-0110-battery/`) uses a single `max_seconds=3600` for every arm. Measured per-step cost at current load, and the 1800-step projection:

| arm | s/step | 1800-step projection | vs 3600 s cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| C6-matched (control, layers=6) | 1.06 | ~1910 s | safe |
| C2-matched (control, layers=2) | 2.35 | ~4230 s | **TRUNCATES** |
| **G-rrarra (geometric)** | **3.70–3.71** | **~6700 s** | **TRUNCATES** |

**The geometric arm is 3.5× the cheapest arm's per-step cost**, because `rrarra` runs 4 recurrence + 2 read layers against the control's transformer stack. One cap cannot serve both, and 3600 serves neither safely.

**A truncated run is VOID, not weak**: `cosine_rate(..., s.steps, step)` still anneals over 1800 (`mqar-bench.rs:1863`), so a run stopped at ~step 970 is not a budget-matched comparison. The battery is therefore on track to complete the **control arm at n=3 and the geometric arm at n=0**, which does not satisfy D20 §2 condition 2 (≥3 seeds) and cannot answer condition 1.

**The remedy is a cap change, not a re-run**: `max_seconds` is a truncation guard, not a recipe parameter — raising it alters no result. The geometric arm needs **≥8000 s**. Two grounded runs (`G-rrarra-s2`, `G-rrarra-s1r`) were stopped early on this reasoning and their partial roots preserved as `*-TRUNCATED-early-stop`, which is accurate labelling rather than a result.

## 2. The hidden-probe measurement is an INSTRUMENT ARTEFACT and must not be reported

`hidden_probe_analysis.json` reports `verdict: BETWEEN` with `h1_ratio_key = 29.54`, CI95 `[20.21, 51.20]`, `ci_excludes_one: true`. **It is an artefact, and the run's own control arms prove it:**

| arm | key top-1 | value top-1 |
|---|---|---|
| h1_cos_age0 (hidden state) | **0.16666666666666666** | 0.0 |
| h2_cos_centred_age0 | **0.16666666666666666** | 0.0 |
| **h3_cos_randproj32 × 5 seeds** | **0.16666666666666666** (all five) | 0.0 |
| h4_cos_first32_age0 | **0.16666666666666666** | 0.0 |
| h5_dot_hidden_age0 | **0.16666666666666666** | 0.0 |
| h6_value_input_cos_age0 | **0.16666666666666666** | 0.0 |
| qk_cos_age / qk_cos_age0 | 0.0039 / 0.0056 | 0.0295 / 0.0143 |

**Five independent RANDOM projections return exactly the same number as the real hidden state, to sixteen digits.** Random projections carry no content identity, so if the hidden state did, h3 would sit near chance while h1 rose. Identical values mean the hidden-space readout is returning a **constant**, not measuring content: it is distance-invariant (1/6 in every bucket d16/d64/d200/d400), lands on a clean rational, and has a **zero-width bootstrap CI**.

**Consequence:** the measurement answers **nothing** about whether the read's q/k projections discard content identity. The honest verdict is instrument failure, not `BETWEEN`. The q/k arms remain the only interpretable numbers and are consistent with the norm-split result (keys flat and near chance, values weakly above).

**The generalisable point:** an agent built five random-projection controls and they demolished its own headline. A 29.5× ratio with a CI excluding 1 would otherwise have gone into the record as a discovery. This is the strongest argument in this session for D20 §2 condition 1's insistence on a matched control rather than a comparison against the incumbent.
